4. Defendant Nos. 1-3, 7 and 4-5 filed 3 separate written statements in the suit. The case of the defendant Nos. 1-3 is that 43 acres of land of suit C.S. Plot No.39 were acquired by the Government in L.A. Case No.71/1964-1965 for Roads and Highways Department and possession thereof was delivered to the Railway Department. Of the total acquired 43 acres of land, 19.94 acres were derequisitioned on 10.04.1980 and the possession thereof was delivered in favour of defendant Nos. 4 and 5 as affected owners of the suit property. The said property is not the khas land of the Government and when it came to the notice of the authority that 5.94 acres of land were settled in favour of plaintiffs as landless people, their settlements were cancelled and proposal was made to grant settlement from other khas land. The proposal for settlement in favour of plaintiffs is under process. The authority rightly cancelled the settlement of the plaintiffs and passed order not to deliver physical possession of the suit property to the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs have not acquired any right to and title in the suit land. The Government did not have the right to grant settlement of the private land in favour of the landless people as khas land. The plaintiffs are not entitled to any relief in the suit. 

 6. The case of defendant Nos.4 and 5 is that according to S.A. Khatian the suit land belonged to Hazi Yeasin, Zahuruddin, Zamiruddin, Miazuddin and others. In 1965 the Government had acquired 43 acres of land of C.S. Plot No. 39 by L.A. Case No.71. Zahuruddin transferred 3.36 acres of land to his sons Saheb Ali and others by a deed of sale dated 04.01.1947. Saheb Ali and others transferred the same to one Ratan Petra by a registered deed of sale dated 17.06.1974. Subsequently, Ratan Petra transferred the same to defendant No. 5 by a deed of sale dated 17.03.1980. Bellla and others, sons of Yeasin Haji, had been in possession of the land of S.A. Khatian No.33. They transferred 3.72 acres of land to Tapan Chowdhury by a registered deed dated 01.07.1974 and they also transferred 3.72 acres of land to Swapan Chowdhury on the same date. Tapan Chowdhury and Shapan Chowdhury transferred 3.61 acres of land each to defendant No.4 by registered deeds dated 19.03.1980 and 17.03.1980 respectively. On 15.02.1980, Zamiruddin transferred .33 acre of land to Soheli who transferred the same to defendant No.4 by a registered deed dated 04.03.1980. Zamiruddin transferred .66 acre of land to Ehsan and Sultan Ahmed by the deed dated 15.02.1980 and Ehsan and Sultan Ahmed also transferred their purchased land to defendant No.4 by registered deed dated 14.03.1980. Abdul Gani, son of Zamiruddin, and Sahera Khanam wife of Hazrat Ali transferred some land to Nilufer Begum who transferred .18 acre of land to defendant No.5 by the deed dated 20.03.1980. Abdul Gani sold .44 acre of land to Mostafa Kamal by registered deed dated 15.02.1980 and Mostafa Kamal subsequently transferred the same to defendant No.5 by a registered deed dated 14.03.1980. Surjaban, wife of Raisuddin, sold .66 acre of land to Abdul Matin by a registered deed dated 05.02.1980 and Zamiruddin also sold .66 acre of land to Abdul Matin. After that, Abdul Matin sold .14 acre of land to defendant No.5 by a registered deed dated 26.04.1980 and delivered possession thereof. Kafiluddin and Aminul Haque transferred 1.92 acres of land to Sirajuddin on 15.01.1980 and Aminul Haque and Sirajuddin transferred 3.84 acres of land to defendant No.4 by a deed dated 12:03.1980 from suit plot No.39. Miazuddin and Malekjan transferred 2.16 acres of land of plot No.39 to Sarafat Ali alias Nur Mohammad Khan by a deed of sale dated 05.02.1980 and Malekjan sold 2.16 acres of land to defendant No. 5 by the deed dated 05.02.1980. While defendant Nos.4 and 5 were in possession of their purchased land of C.S. Plot No.39, the authority by memo dated 21.03.1980 directed to de-requisition the furnished land of the suit plot No.39 to handover to the original owners. Defendant Nos.4 and 5 were asked by the notice dated 14.06.1982 to return the money which they received as compensation from the authority. Defendant Nos. 4 and 5 mutated their names and 5.94 acres of land were settled in favour of plaintiffs but possession thereof was not delivered to them. The proposal for settlement was rightly cancelled. Defendant Nos. 4 and 5 returned the entire compensation money on 01.09.1980 and accordingly, possession of 19.84 acres of land was delivered to them on 28.04.1981. Defendant Nos.4 and 5 have been in possession of 16 annas land from before and they have acquired valid right and title in the said land. The suit land is not the khas land of the Government and as such the settlements of the plaintiffs were rightly cancelled. Meanwhile, the proposal has been made for granting settlement of different lands in favour of plaintiffs. The suit is false and the same is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. Mr. M.A. Samad, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the Government initially cancelled the allotment of landless allottees by making decision to give them alternative khas land without canceling their registered deeds which the Government can do under Rule 103 of the Manual of 1987 and against such decision of the Government, one is under the legal obligation to file appeal before the concerned Divisional Commissioner, if aggrieved and as such the suit and the appeal filed by them are all premature because no cause of action arose as yet to file a declaratory suit I le further submits that the plaintiffs could neither prove their title nor possession in the suit land and that without reversing findings, on those issues of the trial Court, the high Court Division decreed the suit. He also submits that the plaintiffs staled to have taken possession of the suit land before registration of the deeds of lease and that the High Court Division failed to consider that nobody could take possession of khas land without registration of the deed of lease.
